caption:
I ranked 6 tax moves for business owners, legally. General info, 2026–27 rules.

S: Your own super. Up to $32,500 a year in concessional contributions, taxed at 15% in the fund instead of your marginal rate. The catch: it's locked away until you retire.

A: The $20,000 instant asset write-off. Deduct an asset in full in the year you first use it (turnover under $10 million). The catch: you still pay for the asset.

A: The right structure. A base rate entity company pays 25%; a sole trader's top rate is 45%. The catch: getting money out, Division 7A and extra compliance. Worth paying a registered adviser to set up properly.

B: The small business tax offset. Up to $1,000 off for sole traders and partners, automatically.

C: Prepaying. Up to 12 months of expenses early. It moves a deduction forward; it doesn't create one.

D: Buying things to claim them. A dollar spent to save about 30 cents.

It's a general view of how much each can move the bill. Your order depends on profit, cash flow and plans.

Would you rank them differently?

figures_checked: Concessional contributions cap $32,500 for 2026–27 (ATO Key super rates and thresholds, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Sole traders and partners can't pay themselves a salary or wage: any nominal payment is a distribution of profit; a sole trader can usually claim a deduction for their own super contributions (ATO Deductions for salaries, wages and super contributions, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Instant asset write-off: assets costing less than $20,000 each, permanent from 1 July 2026, aggregated turnover under $10 million, first used or installed ready for use in the year (ATO Small business newsroom, updated 4 Sept 2026, checked 15 Nov 2026)
Company tax: base rate entity 25% (turnover under $50 million, passive income 80% or less), 2026–27 (ATO Company tax rate changes, checked 11 Nov 2026)

Resident rates 2026–27: nil to $18,200; 15c to $45,000; $4,020 + 30c to $135,000; $31,020 + 37c to $190,000; $51,370 + 45c above; Medicare levy 2% not included (ATO Tax rates – Australian residents, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Small business income tax offset: 16% of tax on net small business income, capped at $1,000, aggregated turnover under $5 million, sole traders and partners only, 2026–27 (ATO Small business income tax offset, checked 15 Nov 2026)
Prepaid expenses 12-month rule for small business: service period 12 months or less, ending by the end of the next income year (ATO Deductions for prepaid expenses 2026, checked 12 Nov 2026)
